title: The Human Genome Project
text: The Human Genome Project (HGP) was an international scientific research project that successfully mapped and sequenced all of the genes in the human genome. Launched in 1990 and completed in 2003, it was one of the largest collaborative biology projects in history, involving institutions from the United States, United Kingdom, France, Germany, Japan, and China. The project determined that the human genome contains approximately 20,000–25,000 protein-coding genes, far fewer than the 100,000 estimated before the project. The HGP has revolutionized medicine by enabling the identification of genes associated with diseases and paved the way for personalized medicine and pharmacogenomics.
